svg.title: Allocate Capital Before Funding Advertising Expansion
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Capital Before Funding Advertising Expansion; subtitle: Four buckets across $15,000, $45,000, and $80,000 startup envelopes.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values encode the $45,000 planning stack in USD. Each stage also states its $15,000 and $80,000 comparison allocations. These are startup funding envelopes, not the Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual revenue scenarios.; caption: Lean: $6,000 + $3,000 + $2,000 + $4,000 = $15,000. Planning: $18,000 + $9,000 + $7,000 + $11,000 = $45,000. Expanded: $32,000 + $16,000 + $12,000 + $20,000 = $80,000.; stages: label: Opening inventory and supplier purchase commitments; value: Lean $6,000; planning $18,000; expanded $32,000; numeric value: 18000.0; detail: Fund initial authorized-dealer test batches and supplier deposits with SKU-level sell-through limits. Keep purchase cash outflow separate from cost of goods recognized when products sell.; label: Acquisition testing and launch creative production; value: Lean $3,000; planning $9,000; expanded $16,000; numeric value: 9000.0; detail: Release spend in measured cohorts across creative, product pages, and paid traffic. Stop additional funding when retained-order contribution fails the underwriting target.; label: Storefront, integrations, and fulfillment onboarding setup; value: Lean $2,000; planning $7,000; expanded $12,000; numeric value: 7000.0; detail: Budget Shopify configuration, 3PL onboarding, product data, routing tests, and returns setup. Separate one-time implementation payments from recurring software and service expenses.; label: Operating liquidity and exception recovery reserve; value: Lean $4,000; planning $11,000; expanded $20,000; numeric value: 11000.0; detail: Hold cash for settlement delays, replacements, refunds, and operating expenses. Against the canonical $4,000–$25,000 monthly opex range, the planning and expanded reserves bridge initial settlement float before repeat-cohort replenishment.
